concept: The story is a stalemate of nerves: three games, three draws. The hero runs the Krayon grey-to-white flip (Three games. Three draws. / Nobody has blinked yet.) with the scoreline 1.5-1.5 and the 11 games left as the facts. Slide 2 turns the last two games into move-count bars so the 20-move Game 2 sits as a stub against the 60-move Game 3, which shows at a glance that this draw was a fight. caption:
Three games. Three draws. Nobody has blinked in Geneva.

Gukesh held Javokhir Sindarov to a 60-move draw with Black in Game 3 of the World Chess Championship. The score is 1.5-1.5.

Gukesh went for the Berlin Defence and was ready for it. Sindarov burned a lot of his clock in the opening. Engines gave White an edge at times but Gukesh kept finding the moves and was ahead on the clock in the rook and opposite-coloured bishops endgame.

Why so long? Players can't agree a draw before move 40. Game 2 ended in 20 moves only through threefold repetition.

11 games left. First to 7.5 points is champion. Friday is the first rest day and Gukesh has White in Game 4.

Who wins the first game: Gukesh or Sindarov? Tell us below.
